claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 800 MPa room-temperature yield strength.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has an approximately 423 MPa compressive strength at 1273 K at about 30% strain.
The proposed intervention is addition of 0.5–1 at% carbon to TiVNbTa during processing.
Adding 0.5–1 at% carbon to TiVNbTa will produce fine, coherent carbide nanoprecipitates within its BCC matrix.
The carbide nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion, particularly at elevated temperature.
Precipitate-induced obstruction of dislocations will enhance the high-temperature strength of carbon-modified TiVNbTa.
The carbide nanoprecipitates will stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure by limiting grain growth or phase coarsening.
The proposed precipitate dispersion will not compromise the thermal conductivity needed for efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
Carbon modification will increase TiVNbTa yield and compressive strengths at 1273 K by approximately 20–30% relative to the stated baseline.
Carbon-modified TiVNbTa will retain acceptable high-temperature ductility.
Carbon-modified TiVNbTa will retain thermal transport properties within the operational limits of adjoining W and CuCrZr components.
The predicted benefit depends on forming a controlled nanoprecipitate dispersion without deleterious phases.
Unfavorable precipitation or phase changes can reduce ductility severely.
The beneficial effects must persist under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading representative of divertor operation.
Absence of coherent nanoprecipitates in the carbon-added alloys would invalidate the proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 20–30% strength increase, but the falsification rule rejects only results lacking a greater-than-10% increase. An improvement between 10% and 20% would miss the stated prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
